title: Econ Onramp: starter batch/caching defaults and lite-quant autoscaler
author: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Adds an 'Econ Onramp' pathway to ship small-tenant friendly defaults for batching and prefix caching plus a lightweight, conservative quantization autoscaler ('lite-quant') with telemetry-driven rollouts and safety gates. Motivation: Many small customers and PoCs waste cost due to conservative global defaults or risky one-size-fits-all quantization suggestions. This patch provides a low-friction starter configuration that safely reduces per-token cost, gives clear opt-in via CLI/console, and exposes unit-econ telemetry so SRE/Product can monitor regressions. Scope: config presets, simple autoscaler service, CLI opt-in flag, server-side safety checks, telemetry and eval hooks, and docs/examples for onboarding. Not included: full tenant-customization UI and multi-tenant quota enforcement (follow-ups planned). Checklist: [x] presets for batch_size/cache_ttl/kv_prefill; [x] lite-quant autoscaler with snapshot-based conservatism; [x] canary rollout wiring and A/B assignment; [x] telemetry for unit-econ and quality regressions; [x] CLI flag and quickstart example; [x] docs and changelog entries. Risk notes: Lite-quant is conservative by design (no forced re-quantize on production without manual tenant opt-in), quality measurement hooks are required on tenant side for aggressive ramps. How it works (high-level): 1) Onramp presets: a small JSON config shipped under /configs/econ_onramp.json that suggests batch target ranges, cache TTL defaults, and a prefill strategy optimized for short-sequence OLTP workloads; 2) Lite-quant autoscaler: stateless controller that watches sampled inference traces and suggests a quant-tier for tenant traffic with a confidence score; suggestions are stored as draft profiles that require tenant CLI/console approval or an explicit opt-in flag for automatic application; 3) Safety: server-side validators simulate a short shadow-run with the suggested quant tier on a sampled subset and compare token-level perplexity proxy and smoke-test prompts before applying to production; fallback to higher-precision variant if any regression exceed thresholds; 4) Telemetry: new unit_econ metrics (cost_per_k_token, latency_p95_by_quant, quality_probe_failures) and alert thresholds. Merge outcome: squash-merged to main after two approvals and green CI; canary staged to 10% tenants for 48h before global opt-in promotion. Release notes: new 'Econ Onramp' starter profiles and `--econ-onramp` CLI flag; lite-quant autoscaler in beta behind a feature gate; telemetry metrics and alerting dashboards added. Follow-ups: UI to review suggested quant tiers, tenant-level tuning CLI, expand preset coverage for long-sequence workloads, automated rollback playbooks.

Author (Asha): Addressed naming nits and added policy plumbing; exposed SAFETY_QUANT_DELTA env var and added structured logs for shadow-run comparisons.
Sofia Nguyen: Approved after seeing added e2e smoke tests and dashboard wiring. Requested follow-up ticket to add UI review flow.
Daniel Park: Noted CI flake on one test run; re-ran and green. Suggested limiting default canary to 5% for specific regions; updated rollout config to support region-scoped canaries.

release_notes: Introduces 'Econ Onramp' starter profiles (batching/cache defaults) and a conservative 'lite-quant' suggestion engine. Beta behind feature gate. New CLI flag --econ-onramp for tenant opt-in and telemetry metrics under unit_econ.*. Recommended for PoCs and small tenants to reduce per-token cost safely.
notes_for_ops: Canary target default is 10% of eligible tenants for 48h; region-scoped canary supported via rollout config. If quality_probe_failures > 0.5% for 10m, autoscaler suggestions are paused and previous profiles restored. See observability/metrics/unit_econ.promql and telemetry runbook.
